note: Adult-onset SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy mimics IBM clinically, but reports highlight MRI involvement of sartorius and gracilis alongside distinct clinical profiles.

evidence.text: Muelas et al. describe adult-onset SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy presenting with proximo-distal and axial weakness reminiscent of inclusion body myositis, but showing muscle MRI involvement of sartorius and gracilis muscles.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: Muscle MRI identified involvement in the paravertebral, triceps brachii, sartorius and gracilis muscles... We advise SNUPN testing in patients with late-onset proximo-distal and axial weakness with early respiratory impairment and features reminding inclusion body myositis (IBM).

evidence.text: Inclusion body myositis characteristically affects deep finger flexors and knee extensors, serving as a key clinical hallmark.

source.title: Current biomarkers in inclusion body myositis
source.quote: IBM is characterized by weakness in the knee extensor and deep finger flexor muscles due to muscle atrophy and fibroadipose replacement.
